svg.title: The code and the data CyberAPI shares between the desktop app and the web version
svg.desc: The CyberAPI UI and the HTTP engine are code written once and compiled into more than one program. The desktop app is one native process holding the UI and the engine: the UI sends through the engine in-process and keeps projects in a local SQLite file. In the web version the same UI runs as WebAssembly in a browser tab and calls cyberapi-bridge over HTTPS; the bridge sends the requests with the same HTTP engine and keeps the team's projects, accounts and histories in PostgreSQL or MySQL. The desktop app can sign in to the same bridge: it keeps an offline copy of the team's projects in its SQLite file and syncs it when you choose. MCP clients such as Claude Code and Cursor read the same projects through the bridge. The desktop app and the bridge each send to your APIs — REST, GraphQL, gRPC, event streams — on their own.
svg.text: Two ways to run CyberAPI: the same code, the same projects

g.aria-label: A request's path: in-process inside the desktop app, kept in its SQLite file; over HTTPS from the browser tab to cyberapi-bridge, kept in PostgreSQL or MySQL; HTTP from each program to your APIs; the desktop's copy synced with the bridge; MCP clients reading through the bridge

svg.text: THE SAME CODE, COMPILED INTO EACH
